import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def longest_increasing_subsequence_precond (seq : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start auxcode
noncomputable section

/-- Auxiliary copy of strict increase on natural-number index lists,
    available before the official postcondition predicates are declared. -/
def lis_inc_nat (l : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i < j → i < l.length → j < l.length → l.getD i 0 < l.getD j 0

/-- Auxiliary copy of strict increase of values along indices. -/
def lis_inc_vals (seq : List Int) (indices : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i < j → i < indices.length → j < indices.length →
    seq.getD (indices.getD i 0) 0 < seq.getD (indices.getD j 0) 0

/-- Auxiliary validity predicate, used to define the result before the official
    postcondition predicates are declared. -/
def lis_valid_is (seq : List Int) (indices : List Nat) : Prop :=
  lis_inc_nat indices ∧
  (∀ i, i ∈ indices → i < seq.length) ∧
  lis_inc_vals seq indices

@[simp]
lemma lis_valid_is_nil (seq : List Int) : lis_valid_is seq [] := by
  simp [lis_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, lis_inc_vals]

/-- The finite set of all lengths of valid increasing subsequences. It is finite
    because every valid index list has length at most `seq.length`; nevertheless
    we include only lengths in `range (seq.length + 1)`. -/
def lisCandidates (seq : List Int) : Finset Nat := by
  classical
  exact
    (Finset.range (seq.length + 1)).filter
      (fun k => ∃ sub : List Nat, lis_valid_is seq sub ∧ sub.length = k)

lemma lisCandidates_nonempty (seq : List Int) : (lisCandidates seq).Nonempty := by
  classical
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  simp [lisCandidates]

/-- The LIS length, specified as the maximum candidate length. -/
def lisLength (seq : List Int) : Nat :=
  (lisCandidates seq).max' (lisCandidates_nonempty seq)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def longest_increasing_subsequence (seq : List Int)
    (h_precond : longest_increasing_subsequence_precond seq) : Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  lisLength seq
  -- !benchmark @end code

/-
  Post‑condition auxiliary predicates.
-/

/-- `inc_nat l` states that the list `l` of natural numbers is strictly increasing. -/
def inc_nat (l : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i < j → i < l.length → j < l.length → l.getD i 0 < l.getD j 0

/-- `inc_vals seq indices` states that the values of `seq` at the given (strictly increasing)
    indices form a strictly increasing sequence. -/
def inc_vals (seq : List Int) (indices : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i < j → i < indices.length → j < indices.length →
    seq.getD (indices.getD i 0) 0 < seq.getD (indices.getD j 0) 0

/-- `is_valid_is seq indices` bundles the three necessary conditions for a list of indices
    to represent a valid increasing subsequence of `seq`. -/
def is_valid_is (seq : List Int) (indices : List Nat) : Prop :=
  inc_nat indices ∧
  (∀ i, i ∈ indices → i < seq.length) ∧
  inc_vals seq indices

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def longest_increasing_subsequence_postcond
    (seq : List Int) (result : Nat)
    (h_precond : longest_increasing_subsequence_precond seq) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ sub : List Nat, is_valid_is seq sub → sub.length ≤ result) ∧
  (∃ sub : List Nat, is_valid_is seq sub ∧ sub.length = result)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma list_getD_mem_nat (l : List Nat) {i : Nat} (hi : i < l.length) :
    l.getD i 0 ∈ l := by
  induction l generalizing i with
  | nil =>
      simp at hi
  | cons a t ih =>
      cases i with
      | zero =>
          simp [List.getD]
      | succ i =>
          have hi' : i < t.length := Nat.succ_lt_succ_iff.mp hi
          have hmem : t.getD i 0 ∈ t := ih hi'
          simp [List.getD]
          right
          simpa [List.getD] using hmem

lemma lis_valid_is_iff_is_valid_is (seq : List Int) (sub : List Nat) :
    lis_valid_is seq sub ↔ is_valid_is seq sub := by
  simp [lis_valid_is, is_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, inc_nat, lis_inc_vals, inc_vals]

lemma valid_indices_length_le {seq : List Int} {indices : List Nat}
    (h : is_valid_is seq indices) :
    indices.length ≤ seq.length := by
  rcases h with ⟨hinc, hbound, _⟩
  let f : Fin indices.length → Fin seq.length := fun i =>
    ⟨indices.getD i.val 0, hbound _ (list_getD_mem_nat indices i.isLt)⟩
  have hinj : Function.Injective f := by
    intro a b hab
    apply Fin.ext
    by_contra hne
    have hv : indices.getD a.val 0 = indices.getD b.val 0 := by
      exact congrArg Fin.val hab
    rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
    · have hltv := hinc a.val b.val hlt a.isLt b.isLt
      omega
    · have hltv := hinc b.val a.val hgt b.isLt a.isLt
      omega
  have hcard := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hinj
  simpa using hcard

lemma lisCandidates_mem_of_valid {seq : List Int} {sub : List Nat}
    (h : is_valid_is seq sub) :
    sub.length ∈ lisCandidates seq := by
  classical
  have hlen : sub.length ≤ seq.length := valid_indices_length_le h
  have hvalid_lis : lis_valid_is seq sub := by
    simpa [lis_valid_is, is_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, inc_nat, lis_inc_vals, inc_vals] using h
  simp [lisCandidates]
  constructor
  · omega
  · exact ⟨sub, hvalid_lis, rfl⟩

lemma valid_length_le_lisLength {seq : List Int} {sub : List Nat}
    (h : is_valid_is seq sub) :
    sub.length ≤ lisLength seq := by
  classical
  have hmem : sub.length ∈ lisCandidates seq := lisCandidates_mem_of_valid h
  have hle := Finset.le_max' (lisCandidates seq) sub.length hmem
  simpa [lisLength] using hle

lemma exists_valid_length_lisLength (seq : List Int) :
    ∃ sub : List Nat, is_valid_is seq sub ∧ sub.length = lisLength seq := by
  classical
  have hmem : lisLength seq ∈ lisCandidates seq := by
    simpa [lisLength] using
      (Finset.max'_mem (lisCandidates seq) (lisCandidates_nonempty seq))
  rw [lisCandidates, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range] at hmem
  rcases hmem with ⟨_, hprop⟩
  rcases hprop with ⟨sub, hvalid_lis, hlen⟩
  refine ⟨sub, ?_, hlen⟩
  simpa [lis_valid_is, is_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, inc_nat, lis_inc_vals, inc_vals] using hvalid_lis
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem longest_increasing_subsequence_postcond_satisfied
    (seq : List Int) (h_precond : longest_increasing_subsequence_precond seq) :
    longest_increasing_subsequence_postcond
      seq (longest_increasing_subsequence seq h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  constructor
  · intro sub hsub
    simpa [longest_increasing_subsequence] using
      (valid_length_le_lisLength (seq := seq) (sub := sub) hsub)
  · simpa [longest_increasing_subsequence] using
      (exists_valid_length_lisLength seq)
  -- !benchmark @end proof

  ∀ i j, i < j → i < l.length → j < l.length → l.getD i 0 < l.getD j 0

/-- `inc_vals seq indices` states that the values of `seq` at the given (strictly increasing)
    indices form a strictly increasing sequence. -/
def inc_vals (seq : List Int) (indices : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i < j → i < indices.length → j < indices.length →
    seq.getD (indices.getD i 0) 0 < seq.getD (indices.getD j 0) 0

/-- `is_valid_is seq indices` bundles the three necessary conditions for a list of indices
    to represent a valid increasing subsequence of `seq`. -/
def is_valid_is (seq : List Int) (indices : List Nat) : Prop :=
  inc_nat indices ∧
  (∀ i, i ∈ indices → i < seq.length) ∧
  inc_vals seq indices

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def longest_increasing_subsequence_postcond
    (seq : List Int) (result : Nat)
    (h_precond : longest_increasing_subsequence_precond seq) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ sub : List Nat, is_valid_is seq sub → sub.length ≤ result) ∧
  (∃ sub : List Nat, is_valid_is seq sub ∧ sub.length = result)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

lemma list_getD_mem_nat (l : List Nat) {i : Nat} (hi : i < l.length) :
    l.getD i 0 ∈ l := by
  induction l generalizing i with
  | nil =>
      simp at hi
  | cons a t ih =>
      cases i with
      | zero =>
          simp [List.getD]
      | succ i =>
          have hi' : i < t.length := Nat.succ_lt_succ_iff.mp hi
          have hmem : t.getD i 0 ∈ t := ih hi'
          simp [List.getD]
          right
          simpa [List.getD] using hmem

lemma lis_valid_is_iff_is_valid_is (seq : List Int) (sub : List Nat) :
    lis_valid_is seq sub ↔ is_valid_is seq sub := by
  simp [lis_valid_is, is_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, inc_nat, lis_inc_vals, inc_vals]

lemma valid_indices_length_le {seq : List Int} {indices : List Nat}
    (h : is_valid_is seq indices) :
    indices.length ≤ seq.length := by
  rcases h with ⟨hinc, hbound, _⟩
  let f : Fin indices.length → Fin seq.length := fun i =>
    ⟨indices.getD i.val 0, hbound _ (list_getD_mem_nat indices i.isLt)⟩
  have hinj : Function.Injective f := by
    intro a b hab
    apply Fin.ext
    by_contra hne
    have hv : indices.getD a.val 0 = indices.getD b.val 0 := by
      exact congrArg Fin.val hab
    rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
    · have hltv := hinc a.val b.val hlt a.isLt b.isLt
      omega
    · have hltv := hinc b.val a.val hgt b.isLt a.isLt
      omega
  have hcard := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hinj
  simpa using hcard

lemma lisCandidates_mem_of_valid {seq : List Int} {sub : List Nat}
    (h : is_valid_is seq sub) :
    sub.length ∈ lisCandidates seq := by
  classical
  have hlen : sub.length ≤ seq.length := valid_indices_length_le h
  have hvalid_lis : lis_valid_is seq sub := by
    simpa [lis_valid_is, is_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, inc_nat, lis_inc_vals, inc_vals] using h
  simp [lisCandidates]
  constructor
  · omega
  · exact ⟨sub, hvalid_lis, rfl⟩

lemma valid_length_le_lisLength {seq : List Int} {sub : List Nat}
    (h : is_valid_is seq sub) :
    sub.length ≤ lisLength seq := by
  classical
  have hmem : sub.length ∈ lisCandidates seq := lisCandidates_mem_of_valid h
  have hle := Finset.le_max' (lisCandidates seq) sub.length hmem
  simpa [lisLength] using hle

lemma exists_valid_length_lisLength (seq : List Int) :
    ∃ sub : List Nat, is_valid_is seq sub ∧ sub.length = lisLength seq := by
  classical
  have hmem : lisLength seq ∈ lisCandidates seq := by
    simpa [lisLength] using
      (Finset.max'_mem (lisCandidates seq) (lisCandidates_nonempty seq))
  rw [lisCandidates, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range] at hmem
  rcases hmem with ⟨_, hprop⟩
  rcases hprop with ⟨sub, hvalid_lis, hlen⟩
  refine ⟨sub, ?_, hlen⟩
  simpa [lis_valid_is, is_valid_is, lis_inc_nat, inc_nat, lis_inc_vals, inc_vals] using hvalid_lis
-- !benchmark @end lemma
